hero.headline: 17-year-old in custody after Indian River County shootout with 15-year-old, weapon recovered
hero.teaser: Deputies have taken a 17-year-old suspect into custody and recovered a short-barreled pistol following a shootout with a 15-year-old in a residential neighborhood. Video evidence confirms the two teens fired at each other in the middle of the street.
hero.body:
Deputies with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office took a 17-year-old suspect into custody Thursday morning and recovered a weapon after investigating a shootout with a 15-year-old in a residential neighborhood Wednesday night. Investigators obtained video showing the two teenagers shooting at each other in the roadway in the 1100 block of 12th Court Southwest around 7:30 p.m., according to Kevin Jaworski with the sheriff's office.

 Deputies responded to multiple 911 calls and found bullet casings at the scene. A nearby home and vehicle were struck by gunfire. Authorities released a photo of the recovered weapon, which Jaworski described as a short-barreled pistol. Julio Pitts, a resident in the area, said he was sitting in his living room when the shots rang out.

 Authorities believe the shootout stemmed from an ongoing feud between the two teens. Jaworski said the incident appears to be isolated between the two juveniles with no threat to the community, but called it inherently dangerous because a car and house were hit. Neighbors said detectives were in the area throughout the night gathering evidence, and everyone is relieved no one was injured.

cards.headline: 17-year-old in custody after Indian River County shootout with 15-year-old, weapon recovered
cards.teaser: Deputies have taken a 17-year-old suspect into custody and recovered a short-barreled pistol following a shootout with a 15-year-old in a residential neighborhood. Video evidence confirms the two teens fired at each other in the middle of the street.
cards.body:
Deputies with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office took a 17-year-old suspect into custody Thursday morning and recovered a weapon after investigating a shootout with a 15-year-old in a residential neighborhood Wednesday night. Investigators obtained video showing the two teenagers shooting at each other in the roadway in the 1100 block of 12th Court Southwest around 7:30 p.m., according to Kevin Jaworski with the sheriff's office.

 Deputies responded to multiple 911 calls and found bullet casings at the scene. A nearby home and vehicle were struck by gunfire. Authorities released a photo of the recovered weapon, which Jaworski described as a short-barreled pistol. Julio Pitts, a resident in the area, said he was sitting in his living room when the shots rang out.

 Authorities believe the shootout stemmed from an ongoing feud between the two teens. Jaworski said the incident appears to be isolated between the two juveniles with no threat to the community, but called it inherently dangerous because a car and house were hit. Neighbors said detectives were in the area throughout the night gathering evidence, and everyone is relieved no one was injured.
